title: Terraform State, Drift, and Backends
subtitle: Why state matters, how drift happens, and how backend + locking protect teams

nodes.label: State
nodes.definition: State is Terraform's stored record of the infrastructure it manages.
nodes.whyItMatters: Terraform uses state to know what it already created, what it tracks, and what may need to change.
nodes.safeSentence: State is Terraform's memory of managed infrastructure.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not treat state as a disposable cache. Losing or corrupting it can confuse Terraform.
nodes.interviewAnswer: State maps Terraform configuration to real infrastructure, so Terraform can compare desired configuration with managed reality.

note.summary:
State makes Terraform powerful and risky. Terraform reads .tf files, but also tracks what those files represent in real infrastructure.

Code says: I want this bucket.
State says: that is aws_s3_bucket.example and this specific real object.
Cloud says: here is what exists now.

Terraform compares all three to decide changes.

image.caption: State links configuration to real resources; drift appears when manual changes bypass Terraform.

nodes.label: State Mapping
nodes.definition: State mapping connects Terraform resource addresses to real-world resource identities.
nodes.whyItMatters: Without mapping, Terraform would not know which real object belongs to which resource block.
nodes.safeSentence: State mapping is how Terraform connects code names to real cloud objects.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not assume a resource name in code is enough by itself. Terraform also needs the real platform identity.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Terraform state keeps the binding between a configuration resource and the actual remote object.

note.summary: Example: aws_instance.web must map to one real EC2 instance ID. If mapping is wrong, plans can become surprising or destructive.

nodes.label: Local State
nodes.definition: Local state is state stored on the machine running Terraform, usually in a terraform.tfstate file.
nodes.whyItMatters: Local state is simple for learning but risky for team collaboration.
nodes.safeSentence: Local state may be fine for learning, but teams usually need shared remote state.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not casually email, copy, or manually edit local state files.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Local state is useful for small learning projects, but shared environments usually need a remote backend.

note.summary: Local state is easy to start with, but teams can drift into different realities if state is not shared and protected.

nodes.label: Remote Backend
nodes.definition: A backend controls where Terraform stores state; a remote backend stores state outside the local machine.
nodes.whyItMatters: Remote backends let teams share one trusted state location.
nodes.safeSentence: Remote state helps teams collaborate safely around one shared Terraform state.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not confuse a backend with a provider. Backend stores state; provider talks to the target platform.
nodes.interviewAnswer: In team workflows, remote backends are used so everyone works against the same state instead of separate local files.

note.summary: Backend answers where state lives. Provider answers how resources are managed. They are different responsibilities.

nodes.label: Locking
nodes.definition: Locking prevents multiple Terraform runs from writing state at the same time.
nodes.whyItMatters: Concurrent state writes can corrupt or confuse state.
nodes.safeSentence: State locking protects teams from conflicting Terraform runs.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not bypass locking casually with lock=false.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Locking is important because it prevents two users or pipelines from changing state at the same time.

note.summary: Simple picture: one run holds lock, another run waits/fails instead of writing concurrently. Force-unlock exists but is a careful recovery action.

nodes.label: Sensitive State
nodes.definition: State can contain sensitive information from managed infrastructure.
nodes.whyItMatters: State needs access control because it may expose values that should not be public.
nodes.safeSentence: Terraform state should be protected because it can contain sensitive values.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not commit state files to a public repository.
nodes.interviewAnswer: State should be treated as sensitive and protected with access control, encryption, and disciplined backend choices.

note.summary: Safe habits: keep state out of Git, use controlled remote backends, restrict read access, and avoid careless secret outputs.

nodes.label: Refresh
nodes.definition: Refresh updates Terraform's understanding of real infrastructure before a plan or apply.
nodes.whyItMatters: Terraform needs current information to compare desired configuration with managed reality.
nodes.safeSentence: Refresh helps Terraform compare state with what currently exists.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not assume state is always perfectly current before Terraform checks the real platform.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Refresh is part of how Terraform learns whether the real infrastructure still matches what it expects.

note.summary: Refresh helps plan accuracy by re-checking real resource details through providers before proposing change.

nodes.label: Drift
nodes.definition: Drift happens when real infrastructure changes outside Terraform.
nodes.whyItMatters: Drift creates mismatch between code, state, and real infrastructure.
nodes.safeSentence: Drift means the real environment no longer matches what Terraform expects.
nodes.commonTrap: Manual cloud console changes can create drift if they bypass Terraform.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Drift is when someone changes infrastructure outside the Terraform workflow, causing reality to diverge from the managed configuration.

note.summary: Example: Terraform expects one instance size, manual console edit changes it. Next plan reveals unexpected differences.

nodes.label: Import
nodes.definition: Import connects an existing real-world resource to Terraform state.
nodes.whyItMatters: Import helps bring resources created outside Terraform under Terraform management.
nodes.safeSentence: Import can bring existing resources into Terraform state, but it must be done carefully.
nodes.commonTrap: Import does not automatically write perfect Terraform configuration for you in all workflows.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Import is used when a team wants Terraform to start tracking an existing resource, but the mapping and configuration must be handled carefully.

note.summary: After import, always run and review plan carefully. Mismatched config can trigger unexpected change proposals.

nodes.label: State Commands
nodes.definition: State commands inspect or carefully adjust Terraform state.
nodes.whyItMatters: They can help troubleshoot state, but misuse can cause serious problems.
nodes.safeSentence: Terraform state commands are powerful and should be used carefully.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not manually edit raw state files when safer Terraform state commands exist.
nodes.interviewAnswer: State commands can inspect or adjust state, but they require discipline because state controls Terraform's understanding of managed infrastructure.

note.summary: Common commands: terraform state list, terraform state show, terraform state mv, terraform state rm. Use with review discipline.

nodes.label: State Mistakes
nodes.definition: State mistakes include deleting, corrupting, exposing, or incorrectly modifying Terraform state.
nodes.whyItMatters: Bad state handling can lead to unexpected plans, broken tracking, or security risk.
nodes.safeSentence: State mistakes can be serious, so state operations need discipline and review.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not fix state problems by randomly editing state files.
nodes.interviewAnswer: The safest Terraform teams treat state as a controlled asset, not a throwaway file.

note.summary: Risky behavior includes deleting state blindly, committing it to Git, force-unlocking active runs, or importing to wrong addresses.

nodes.label: Terraform Core Workflow
nodes.definition: Open the previous map that explains the practical Terraform workflow.
nodes.whyItMatters: This gives Sean a doorway back to the workflow map.
nodes.safeSentence: State makes more sense when connected back to the plan, review, and apply workflow.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not mix this navigation bubble with state concepts. It is a map doorway, not a state concept.
nodes.interviewAnswer: State is central to the Terraform workflow because plan and apply rely on Terraform understanding what it already manages.
